messages.subject: stat_smooth function stopped working?
parts:
This has always worked for me and I have various revisions of this same script saved but I now get this error:

geom_smooth: method="auto" and size of largest group is >=1000, so using gam with formula: y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"). Use 'method = x' to change the smoothing method.
geom_smooth: method="auto" and size of largest group is <1000, so using loess. Use 'method = x' to change the smoothing method.
Error in predLoess(object$y, object$x, newx, object$s, object$weights,  : 
  NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 5)
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)
Error in if (nrow(layer_data) == 0) return() : argument is of length zero

I tried uninstalling and reinstalling ggplot2

Code:
bpssc <- read.csv ("bp-join.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",", quote="\"", dec=".",fill = FALSE,colClasses=c("Date"="Date")) 

ggplot<- ggplot(data=bpssc, aes(x=Date,y=BR.Score, group = Unit)) 

ggplot + geom_point(aes(color = BR.Region), size=3.5,alpha = I(.5)) + scale_colour_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2") 

last_plot() + stat_smooth(aes(group = 1),fill = "darkgray", se=TRUE,col="black", size = .9, level =.95,fullrange = FALSE,lty=2) #group 1 GAM all data

last_plot() + stat_smooth(aes(color = BR.Region),fill = "darkgray", se=F, size = 1.9, level =.95,fullrange = TRUE)#trends of individual regions

On Wed, Jan 16, 2013 at 7:48 PM, Kevin <skycon...@gmail.com> wrote:
> This has always worked for me and I have various revisions of this same
> script saved but I now get this error:
>

These are messages informing you that ggplot2 is using gam() to create
the smoothing rather than loess.

> geom_smooth: method="auto" and size of largest group is >=1000, so using gam
> with formula: y ~ s(x, bs = "cs"). Use 'method = x' to change the smoothing
> method.
> geom_smooth: method="auto" and size of largest group is <1000, so using
> loess. Use 'method = x' to change the smoothing method.
This is definitely an error, but it's informative:

> Error in predLoess(object$y, object$x, newx, object$s, object$weights, :
> NA/NaN/Inf in foreign function call (arg 5)

arg 5 is weights, and it's telling you that at least one of the
weights either blew up (Inf), generated an NaN or a missing value (not
uncommon along the extremes if the data in those regions is too
sparse).

> In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first
> 50)
> Error in if (nrow(layer_data) == 0) return() : argument is of length zero

This warning appears to be indicating that at least one of your groups
has no data, but a traceback of the call may be more informative.

>
> I tried uninstalling and reinstalling ggplot2
>
> Code:
> bpssc <- read.csv ("bp-join.csv", header = TRUE, sep = ",", quote="\"",
> dec=".",fill = FALSE,colClasses=c("Date"="Date"))
>
> ggplot<- ggplot(data=bpssc, aes(x=Date,y=BR.Score, group = Unit))
>
> ggplot + geom_point(aes(color = BR.Region), size=3.5,alpha = I(.5)) +
> scale_colour_brewer(type="qual", palette="Dark2")
>
> last_plot() + stat_smooth(aes(group = 1),fill = "darkgray",
> se=TRUE,col="black", size = .9, level =.95,fullrange = FALSE,lty=2) #group 1
> GAM all data
>
> last_plot() + stat_smooth(aes(color = BR.Region),fill = "darkgray", se=F,
> size = 1.9, level =.95,fullrange = TRUE)#trends of individual regions

One guess is that because of the fullrange argument, at least one of
your groups had little or no data in the extremes of the x-range,
which causes the loess/gam algorithm to become sufficiently unstable
to generate NA/NaN/Inf weights. Remember that warning in intro stats
about extrapolating beyond the range of your data? When dealing with
adaptive estimation algorithms, this warning is especially true.

Dennis

Thank you for your thoughtful reply Dennis,
What's interesting about this situation is I'm using the same data set that for weeks has given 3 nice gam lines each colored by region. The Score range is from 0 to 100 but the majority of the scores are over 60 and there are three distinct regions. The score, date, and region columns do not have any NAs, negative values, or something egregiously wrong.

What did you mean by a traceback? I'm not sure how to evaluate the problem further.

Thanks again Dennis!
